A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ONR/OMA/MAT research. All 35 pages in each version, including Appendices A–I, support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures. Appendix content and rendered layout are identical apart from the publication header.

before.justification: v3 reports original MAT evaluations on OMA in Tables 1–6, plus curvature analyses, robustness experiments, and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark comparisons, ablations, robustness experiments, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain the same vector inputs, path-aware and spatial attention, association head, CE-plus-CTC objective, and topology-constrained beam search. No algorithm or architecture change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OMA from nuScenes/OSM in Boston and Singapore, including MapTR, MapTRv2, and SeqGrowGraph perception maps. The nuScenes-C weather scenarios and other perturbed-input evaluations are also retained without changes in coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain HMM, DeepMM, MTrajRec, GraphMM, EAM3, KNN, GMT, and FastMAC. The PTv3 reference in Table 3 and qualitative comparators are unchanged. The newly cited works are not added to evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported splits, training budgets, model configurations, and testing protocols are unchanged. Section 4.2 is shortened but retains the 1 m Chamfer threshold, 50–95% overlap thresholds, and 15 length intervals; the detailed appendix protocols are identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the structural and loss ablations, geographic transfer and data-efficiency experiments, curvature analysis, SD-map perturbations, environmental robustness tests, attention visualizations, and failure cases. Relocated tables do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results, and the statement about releasing random seeds remains identical.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains MAT-T at 78.2 and 34 ms; Table 2 retains MAT-L scores of 41.9, 45.0, and 54.9 for MapTR, MapTRv2, and SeqGrowGraph inputs. Appendix outcomes are identical.

T1.justification: The task definitions, Equations 1–14, metric pseudocode, complexity arguments, and beam-search formulation are retained. Condensing Section 4.2 does not revise the metric's mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same ONR task, first OMA benchmark claim, MAT contribution, NR P-R metric, and low-cost real-time navigation claims. The new conference-publication header does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, data efficiency, attention mechanisms, and robustness are unchanged. Both retain the discussions of geometric complexity, occlusion, localization failures, annotation dependence, and future integration with motion planners.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, annotation procedures, augmentation details, and model configurations remain unchanged in Section 6.1 and the appendices. The repository link and code, annotation, and checkpoint release statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds introductory citations and references to Li et al. (2025), Amap, and Shan et al. (2025), Stability under Scrutiny. Existing research positioning is retained. The SP2T preprint-to-ICCV update refers to the same work and is a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: v4 condenses the three metric-stage explanations in Section 4.2 and makes small wording edits elsewhere. It adds Xinyuan Chang to the displayed author list, expands affiliations and author notes, updates the publication header, and adds acknowledgments. The overall organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 1 to page 2, while Tables 2–4 and 6 move earlier and existing displays are regrouped. Caption styling and main-text pagination receive limited adjustments. No figures or tables are added or redrawn; appendix layouts remain unchanged apart from headers.

improvement.justification: Section 4.2 becomes shorter while preserving its substance, and v4 updates references, front matter, and display placement. These limited editorial changes leave the scientific evidence, reproducibility information, interpretations, and limitations intact, with no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
